{{Short description|Ratio of sample size to population size}}
In [[Statistical sampling|sampling theory]], the '''sampling fraction''' is the ratio of [[sample (statistics)|sample]] size to [[statistical population|population]] size or, in the context of [[stratified sampling]], the ratio of the sample size to the size of the stratum.<ref>{{cite book|last=Dodge|first=Yadolah|title=The Oxford Dictionary of Statistical Terms|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Oxford|date=2003|isbn=0-19-920613-9|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse}}</ref>
The formula for the sampling fraction is
:<math>f=\frac{n}{N},</math>

where ''n'' is the sample size and ''N'' is the population size. A sampling fraction value close to 1 will occur if the sample size is relatively close to the population size. When sampling from a [[finite population]] [[Sampling with replacement|without replacement]], this may cause [[Correlation and dependence|dependence]] between individual samples. To correct for this dependence when calculating the sample [[variance]], a [[finite population correction]] (or finite population multiplier) of <math>\frac{N-n}{N-1}</math> may be used. If the sampling fraction is small, less than 0.05, then the sample variance is not appreciably affected by dependence, and the finite population correction may be ignored. <ref>{{Cite book |title=Introduction to probability and mathematical statistics |last=Bain |first=Lee J. |date=1992 |publisher=PWS-KENT Pub |last2=Engelhardt |first2=Max |isbn=0534929303 |edition=2nd |location=Boston |oclc=24142279}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Elementary survey sampling |url=https://archive.org/details/elementarysurvey00sche_0 |url-access=registration |last=Scheaffer |first=Richard L. |date=2006 |publisher=Thomson Brooks/Cole |last2=Mendenhall |first2=William |last3=Ott |first3=Lyman |isbn=0495018627 |edition=6th |location=Southbank, Vic. |oclc=58425200}}</ref>
